content.text: The text surveys major Civil War campaigns from Chancellorsville through Sherman’s 1864 advance. Jackson’s flank attack routed the Eleventh Corps, but his own troops mortally wounded him; Sedgwick captured Marye’s Heights before retreating, and Hooker withdrew across the Rappahannock after staying at headquarters in the Chancellor house. Grant’s daring Vicksburg campaign captured the city and Port Hudson, securing the Mississippi. Gettysburg, where Meade defeated Lee and Pickett’s Charge failed, marked the Confederacy’s high-water mark. Rosecrans lost Chickamauga, but Thomas held Chattanooga; Grant then captured Lookout Mountain and Missionary Ridge. Grant’s Wilderness and Spotsylvania battles bled Lee, while Cold Harbor and Petersburg followed. Sheridan defeated Early in the Shenandoah, including at Cedar Creek, where he rode from Winchester to rally his army. Sherman flanked Johnston toward Atlanta, captured the city, and began his destructive march to the sea.
